text:
maria: Heads-up — CI perf job flagged a ~25% token/sec drop on canary for continuous-batcher after the last rollout. Rollout is on hold. :eyes:

ci-bot: PERF ALERT: continuous-batcher tokens/sec decreased by 24.7% vs baseline (job: perf/continuous-batcher/weekly)

sahil: ugh. which commit? any obvious kernel changes or batching heuristics in the diff?

maria: bisect in progress, but local microbench shows tokens/sec went 12k -> 9k for typical 512-seq streams. Batch size distribution shifted — more small batches.

alex: paste of `perf/continuous-batcher` run:
```
model: redwood/ggml-4bit
baseline tokens/sec: 12000
canary tokens/sec: 9000
batch hist (baseline): {1: 10%, 2: 25%, 4: 40%, 8+: 25%}
batch hist (canary):   {1: 45%, 2: 30%, 4: 20%, 8+: 5%}
avg queue wait per req: baseline 4ms, canary 32ms
```

vikram: that queue wait jump is suspicious — scheduler seems to be batching less aggressively or letting inflight preemption thrash. Also saw KV-cache miss amplification: canary showed 15% higher kv miss rate on requests that hit reused prefixes.

jen: any kernel selection logs? maybe fallback to slower attention kernels for small seq lengths?

maria: yes. from runtime logs: `kernel_choice: attention_fused -> attention_generic` around commit `9f2b1e3` (PR #4821). PR description was "fallback for attention overflow on some GPUs".

sahil: so PR #4821 changed fallback ordering and also touched the batcher backpressure threshold? I remember a couple lines in scheduler.c about preferred_batch_fill.

maria: exactly. bisect landed us on 9f2b1e3. git bisect summary:
```
$ git bisect start
$ git bisect bad HEAD
$ git bisect good v1.12.3
bisect run: ./scripts/bench/continuous_batcher --short
--> culprit: 9f2b1e3 PR#4821
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY NOTE: canary rollout paused at 2026-03-17T10:12:00 UTC — manual hold by release-engineering

alex: quick experiment — reverted kernel-order change locally and re-ran bench: tokens/sec returned to ~11800 and batch hist looks like baseline. KV miss dropped too.

vikram: so two levers: (1) kernel fallback unintentionally slower (attention_generic deopt path), (2) scheduler heuristics combined with kernel check added extra per-request latency leading to smaller batches. They compounded.

jen: can we hotfix by pinning kernel selection for the fused path and tweak backpressure in scheduler? Which is lower risk?

sahil: pinning kernel order (i.e., prefer fused for known configs) is low-risk and quick revert of PR#4821. We'll open a revert PR and run CI perf.

maria: opened rollback PR #4835 — small revert of the kernel-order change and the scheduler threshold tweak. Running CI now.

ci-bot: CI PERF: PR#4835 run complete — tokens/sec delta +22.1% vs canary (p95 latency down 18%).

jen: nice. keep rollback queued until we confirm no functional regression. Any test failures?

maria: integration smoke looks green. Also added a microprofile to capture KV cache reuse ratio and queue occupancy. Snapshot attached to the ticket.

alex: follow-up: scheduler metrics showed a pathological case where preemption check ran for every inflight request and induced a 20-40us penalty per call which aggregated into 20-30ms queue waits at 3000 rps. Patch in PR#4835 disables that check when batching enabled.

vikram: long-term fix ideas: (a) add a fastpath that short-circuits kernel selection for common model configs (b) make batching policy robust to short-term kernel warmups (prefer delaying small immediate batches by up to X ms to let batches form), (c) improve KV cache warmup telemetry and use it to bias batching.

jen: can you add a small doc/update in eng-runtime on the tradeoffs? this pattern will repeat. Put perf repro steps in bench scripts.

maria: on it. I'll also schedule a short postmortem in eng-runtime sync. For now, rollout remains on hold until prod canaries verify after reverting. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sahil: thumbs up. once rollback merges, let's re-run the broader perf test matrix across GPUs and seq lengths to ensure no hidden regressions.

maria: noted. will coordinate with perf infra to run overnight matrix.

alex: filing follow-up tickets: RT-914 (kernel-selection fastpath), RT-915 (batching-delay-policy), RT-916 (kvcache telemetry).

ops-bot: TICKET CREATED: RT-914, RT-915, RT-916 (assigned to eng-runtime)

maria: end of thread — thanks all.
